conventions: Bare nominal predicates in the antithetical couplet: where an anarthrous participle, adjective or noun is the predicate of a verbless colon, this chapter puts the construction-supplied copula (rule 20), the preposition rule 33 supplies before the bare nominal, and the antecedent-and-relative rule 46 supplies for a substantive all into that one unit, headed on the word carrying the lexeme — 14.22 *shall be to them that devise*, 14.29 *is of great*, 14.35 *against him that causeth shame*, and the *He that is soon/slow/hasty* units of 14.17 and 14.29. The competing reading, splitting the supplied copula off as its own `added` unit, was considered at 14.22 and rejected throughout the chapter.

Supplied English verbs were placed by the subtraction tests of rules 34 and 43 rather than by the ASV's italics, which corroborate and decide nothing (rule 7). *findeth it* (14.6), *tendeth* (14.23), *causeth* (14.25) and *hath* (14.20) are each their own `added` unit, because no morpheme in their clauses is left short when the words are dropped. Against them, *shall be satisfied* (14.14) joins the verb the Hebrew writes once and the ASV realizes in both cola, as one discontinuous unit (rules 25, 34), and *hath a refuge* (14.32) joins the participle the ASV renders by nothing else (rule 43).
report: Read all 35 verses end to end against the 47-lemma candidate table. No construction is analysed two ways without something in the source or the printed ASV licensing the difference, so no patches.

The table's one same-verse flag, HRSH at 14.22, is not a split: colon 1 is a finite clause whose antecedent is the verb's own subject pronoun, so the participle takes only the supplied relative (rule 46); colon 2 is verbless with the participle chain as the bare nominal predicate, so its unit also carries the construction-supplied copula (rule 20), the supplied *to* (rule 33) and the supplied antecedent (rule 46). Same rules, different clause type.

DRK 14.2 *in ways* vs 14.14 *ways* is rule 11 function-word priority, not a split: 14.14 writes MN, which takes the *with*, while 14.2 writes no preposition and the word goes to the nominal (rules 19, 33). HYH 14.23 *there is* (rule 21), 14.26 *shall have* (possessive LE present, rule 43) and 14.35 *will be* (ordinary written verb) are three clause types, not three analyses. The remaining buckets differ only in ASV wording or clause role.

Checked the nine `added` units by reading the dump, since the lemma table is blind to them. They agree with each other: a connective where no waw stands (14.24 *But*, rule 14's closing sentences), supplied lexical verbs (14.6 *findeth it*, 14.23 *tendeth*, 14.25 *causeth*, 14.20 *hath*), and supplied function words no morpheme licenses (14.3 *his*, 14.7 *in him*, 14.24 *only*, 14.33 *that which is*). The one italic verb not marked added, 14.14 *shall be satisfied*, is the second realization of the verb the Hebrew writes once across the couplet (rule 34's pro-verb paragraph) — the correct opposite outcome, not an inconsistency.

Construct-chain determiners are uniform: the single supplied determiner goes to the construct noun whether the construct is the English attributive (14.1 *Every wise*) or the English head (14.5, 14.25, 14.30), and to the possessor where the ASV writes an English possessive (14.28, 14.35 *The king's*). Copula placement is likewise uniform: on the preposition where a prepositional phrase is the predicate (14.4, 14.35) and on the nominal where a nominal predicate stands behind a fronted phrase (14.3, 14.26, 14.28), which is rule 49's closing paragraph.

BSB disagreements (5): none is a genuine error. Three are LE left unrepresented — a bare English object at 14.15 and 14.21, and 14.26 where HYH takes the *have* and the preposition keeps nothing (rules 40, 43). The other two are ASV elisions: NPSH in 14.10, where *its own bitterness* writes no *soul* and *own* belongs to the suffix (rule 18), and the suffix of AHRYTH in 14.13, where *the end of mirth* writes no pronoun (rule 22). No accepted edge was changed.

Promotions: none. The bare-nominal-predicate bundle is already decided by rules 20, 33 and 46; the italic-verb split by rule 34's pro-verb paragraph and rule 43's subtraction test. The one uncovered form is the positive existential YSH at 14.12 (*There is a way*, headed on *is*), and one occurrence with no corpus precedent in the packet is too thin to bind later chapters — rules 21 and 50 already determine it by analogy.

Two conventions recorded, both judgments a later Proverbs chapter would otherwise re-derive: the bare-nominal-predicate bundling, whose competing reading the 14.22 verse pass itself named, and which supplied English verbs were folded in versus left `added`.
